key_insight: An end-to-end DFT-to-Wannier-to-ADAPT-VQE pipeline can prepare active-space Hamiltonians for strongly correlated materials, but classical cost rises sharply as the active space grows.
engineering_relevance: The work provides a practical benchmark for hybrid quantum-classical materials workflows, helping engineers estimate memory, runtime, and scalability limits before deployment.
method: DFT geometry relaxation and NSCF calculations to generate electronic structure inputs
Wannier-based orbital localization to define active-space Hamiltonians
ADAPT-VQE accelerated with GOCP and O(5) Taylor-expanded operator evolution
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a benchmark on Li-hBN with active spaces expanded from 8 to 14 spatial orbitals, revealing a critical scaling wall where simulation becomes intractable.
watch_item: Results are benchmark-specific and may not generalize across materials, hardware backends, or larger active spaces without additional error and resource analysis.
paper_title: An Integrated DFT-Wannier-Quantum Embedding Pipeline for Strongly Correlated Materials: Scaling Benchmarks in Li-hBN
